questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that the university is known for having a good environmental studies programme and the amount of interesting classes I could take there. It was also important for me to be able to experience and explore another kind of nature than I'm used to and the possibilities for that are many on Vancouver Island!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. They provide you with all the information in e-mails well in time and if you're in doubt about something they will answer fairly quickly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails also after my arrival. Apart from that I joined the welcome activities for international students, that was very helpful! They show you around and make sure to facilitate meetings between between students which in my opinion is important for a good exchange stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was searching via different Facebook-groups before finding something elsewhere. It can take a bit of time, but don't give up! Try and connect with other Danes going there and ask if they know someone or found something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked living off campus. Transport to and from campus takes a bit longer obviously, but I was glad that all of my daily life did not take place on campus. You can rent a bike through the BikeHub at the university, would recommend that! That makes transportation easy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was super happy with where I lived! But Victoria can be hard to find (affordable) housing in.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a bit long, but they help you all the way through.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I filled out a registration form in spring (spring right before the autumn of my exchange) and got my Letter of Acceptance in May. Then I could start looking for classes. Registration for classes was in start/mid June.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom-meetings, e-mailing and a website that provides step-by-step guides for registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had some trouble getting the classes I wanted because I had to replace some compulsory classes in my home university. It ended up working out, and I got some other classes instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient! And take it one step at a time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My impression was that the level of the courses was generally lower than in my home university. We worked differently though, there was a lot of small assignments throughout the semester, so I'd say that the effort it takes is about the same.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More work throughout the semester and more focus on details and remembering a lot of texts at the same time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Biodiversity and Conservation Biology, Environmental Management, Ethnoecology and Introduction to Ceramics Wheels and Hand Techniques

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ethnoecology was great! You learn a lot about the First Nations of Canada and the way they have stewarded and taken care of the land. Environmental management was also great, the professor is super nice and the class is very broad and comes around many interesting topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries are quite expensive on the island

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A bit more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UVic has so many opportunities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs ranging from sports clubs, craft clubs, hiking/outdoor clubs, academic clubs, religious clubs, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join Clubs and Unions Day at the beginning of the semester. That's a great way to experience just how many clubs there actually are and also to meet the people behind the clubs. I joined the Ecological Restoration club and went a trip with them and met the nicest people. The outdoor club is also cool!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and go out to explore the island! It's cheap to rent a car and easy to get around. Join clubs and be open to meeting new people! Don't go alone! Nature is different over there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Canadians are super welcoming and kind.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be brave and open. It's a cliché but it works: Put yourself out there!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only small differences as the humor. But you will quickly adjust.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and that they're always willing to help you. I experienced this throughout my whole stay.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Participate in the welcoming activities for international students! Remember to relax sometimes :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not other that the above mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met there! Will cherish that forever

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing resting and exploring and academic work.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
